Can blocking an exit get more people out?
In a panic, the crowd locks into an arch at the door. Only 52 get out.
Add a V-shaped splitter. It cuts the crowd into two streams, and 94 get out. Nearly double.
Too close, and the gap pinches shut. The splitter becomes the bottleneck. Just 18.
Too far back, and the streams merge again before the door. It barely helps.
Make it flat, and the crowd hits it head-on. No better than nothing.
At forty-five degrees, one metre back, everyone is out in two minutes two, not two minutes fifty-eight.
This is the exit paradox. The right obstacle speeds up the exit.
